title: Arbitrary Sensitive File Disclosure via SimpleHTTPRequestHandler Root Directory
description: The backend HTTP server initializes SDUInventoryRequestHandler with directory=PROJECT_ROOT. Because SimpleHTTPRequestHandler recursively serves files directly from this directory without filtering hidden dotfiles or sensitive configuration, unauthenticated remote clients can download secrets including .env (containing database credentials and STAFF_AUTH_SECRET), .git/config, docker-compose.yml, and server source code.
root_cause: backend/server.py:975 configures SimpleHTTPRequestHandler with directory=PROJECT_ROOT without overriding translate_path or filtering forbidden file extensions and directory paths.
intended_behavior: The HTTP server must restrict file serving to safe public web assets (HTML, CSS, JS, images) and strictly block access to hidden files (.env, .git), source directories (backend/, tests/, scripts/), and database scripts.

trace.description: Initializes SimpleHTTPRequestHandler with directory pointing to the repository root directory.
Delegates non-API GET requests directly to super().do_GET() without path or extension filtering.
Translates requested URI to absolute filesystem path and opens the target file for streaming to client.

evidence.description: def do_GET(self): if self.path.startswith('/api'): ... else: super().do_GET()

conditions.description: HTTP server is running and accessible over TCP port 8080.

instructions: Send an HTTP GET request to http://localhost:8080/.env
Send an HTTP GET request to http://localhost:8080/.git/config
execution.observed_result: Server returns HTTP 200 OK with the contents of .env including DB_PASSWORD and STAFF_AUTH_SECRET.

remediation.strategy: Override translate_path in SDUInventoryRequestHandler or validate request paths in do_GET to reject requests for hidden dotfiles, parent directories, and sensitive system files with HTTP 404/403.

likelihood.reason: Direct unauthenticated HTTP GET requests reliably retrieve sensitive files without any special privileges or prerequisite conditions.

impact.reason: Exposure of database credentials and cryptographic secrets allows full administrative compromise of PostgreSQL database and application state.

confidence.reason: Live HTTP GET requests to /.env returned HTTP 200 with sensitive environment secrets.

title: Missing Server-Side Authentication and Authorization on Administrative API Endpoints
description: Administrative actions executed via POST /api (including approveRequisition, completeRequisition, rejectRequisition, restockItem, adjustStock, saveUser, deleteUser, addDepartment, saveItem, deleteItem) are not gated by server-side authentication tokens or authorization checks. Authentication is only verified client-side in staff.html via sessionStorage.
root_cause: backend/server.py:1044-1080 dispatches POST action strings directly to database mutation handlers without verifying a valid session token, authorization header, or secret signature.
intended_behavior: All administrative mutation endpoints must require and verify a valid cryptographic session token or HMAC Bearer token generated upon successful staff authentication before processing privileged operations.

trace.description: Receives JSON payload from unauthenticated caller at /api.
Maps action string to administrative handler functions without checking caller authentication state.
Executes SQL UPDATE and inserts stock transaction records on behalf of an unverified caller.

evidence.description: actions = {'approveRequisition': self.handle_approve_requisition, 'adjustStock': self.handle_adjust_stock, 'saveUser': self.handle_save_user, ...} handler = actions.get(action)

conditions.description: Network access to POST /api endpoint on port 8080.

instructions: Send POST /api with Content-Type: application/json containing an administrative action and no authorization credentials.
execution.observed_result: The server executes the request and returns success status with updated stock quantity.

remediation.strategy: Implement server-side authentication verification in do_POST for all administrative actions, requiring an Authorization Bearer token signed with STAFF_AUTH_SECRET.

likelihood.reason: Administrative endpoints can be invoked by anyone with network reachability using standard HTTP clients.

impact.reason: Allows unauthorized manipulation of stock inventory, approving or rejecting requisitions, and tampering with user accounts.

confidence.reason: Code review confirms absence of authentication middleware in do_POST dispatch table.

title: Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) via Unsanitized Requisition and User Attributes
description: Requisition attributes (such as requester, dept, purpose, and reject_reason) and item names are inserted directly into DOM innerHTML templates in staff.html and index.html without HTML entity escaping. An attacker submitting a requisition with HTML tags can execute arbitrary JavaScript in the context of staff members viewing the requisition queue.
root_cause: staff.html:1081-1083 interpolates user-controlled string properties directly into innerHTML string literals without calling an HTML sanitizer or escape function.
intended_behavior: All dynamic user-controlled strings rendered into the DOM must be properly escaped using an HTML entity encoder (e.g. replacing &, <, >, ", ' with named entities) or inserted via textContent.

trace.description: Collects requester, dept, and purpose values from form inputs and sends to /api.
Stores unsanitized text strings into requisitions database table.
Interpolates raw req.requester and req.purpose values directly into card.innerHTML.

evidence.description: ${vIcons.fileText} วัตถุประสงค์: ${req.purpose}

conditions.description: A staff administrator views pending requisitions on staff.html.

instructions: Submit a requisition with purpose containing ''
Open staff.html and observe the requisition list rendering.
execution.observed_result: Browser interprets raw HTML tags from requisition purpose and executes inline JavaScript in staff portal origin.

remediation.strategy: Define an escapeHtml helper function and wrap all untrusted requisition and inventory field interpolations across staff.html and index.html.

likelihood.reason: Requires submitting a requisition containing payload and an administrator viewing the dashboard.

impact.reason: Allows execution of arbitrary JavaScript within staff portal context, enabling session hijacking and unauthorized API invocations.

confidence.reason: Inspection of staff.html template strings confirms direct interpolation of user inputs into innerHTML.

title: Plaintext Password Storage and Insecure Hardcoded Fallback Credentials
description: User account passwords in the users table are stored and compared in plaintext. Additionally, when creating a new user or updating an account without specifying a password, the system falls back to a hardcoded default password 'sdu1234'.
root_cause: backend/server.py:734 sets password = data.get('password') or 'sdu1234' without hashing, and backend/server.py:795 compares password != valid_pass using plaintext string equality.
intended_behavior: User passwords must be salted and hashed using a modern one-way key derivation function (e.g. PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256, bcrypt, or Argon2) prior to storage, and login comparisons must use constant-time cryptographic hash verification.

trace.description: Receives password string from user creation request.
Assigns plaintext password with fallback to 'sdu1234' and persists directly into PostgreSQL users table.
Validates user authentication via direct plaintext comparison if password != valid_pass.

evidence.description: if password != valid_pass: self.send_json_response({'status': 'error', 'message': 'รหัสผ่านไม่ถูกต้อง'}, status_code=401)

conditions.description: Users exist in PostgreSQL users table.

execution.attacker_perspective: Actor with database read access or database backup file
payloads: SELECT id, username, password FROM users;
instructions: Inspect the password column of the users table in database sdu_inventory.
execution.observed_result: Password values appear in cleartext without any hashing or cryptographic protection.

remediation.strategy: Hash user passwords using hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac with SHA-256 and a random 16-byte salt, storing salt and hash in the database, and verify via hmac.compare_digest.

code_changes.fixed_code:
def hash_password(password: str) -> str:
    salt = os.urandom(16)
    dk = hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac('sha256', password.encode(), salt, 600000)
    return f"{salt.hex()}:{dk.hex()}"

likelihood.reason: Requires read access to database, backup archives, or SQL leakage.

impact.reason: Exposes cleartext credentials of all system users, enabling account takeover and credential stuffing.

confidence.reason: Verified directly in backend/server.py:734 and schema_postgres.sql.

title: Permissive Wildcard Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) Policy
description: The backend server includes Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on all HTTP responses, allowing any third-party origin in a client browser to interact with local/intranet API endpoints.
root_cause: backend/server.py:990 sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin to wildcard * unconditionally.
intended_behavior: In production, CORS headers should either restrict allowed origins to an explicit trusted allowlist or be omitted when requests originate from the same host.

trace.description: Invoked during request handling to append cross-origin headers.
Writes header Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * to client response.

conditions.description: An intranet user visits an attacker-controlled website on the same workstation or browser session.

execution.attacker_perspective: Third-party website visited by intranet user
instructions: Initiate a cross-origin XMLHttpRequest or fetch from an external domain to http://localhost:8080/api.
execution.observed_result: Browser permits the cross-origin response reading because of Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *.

remediation.strategy: Restrict CORS origin header to configured domains or remove wildcard in production.

likelihood.reason: Requires an intranet user to open an untrusted webpage while having active network reachability to the server.

impact.reason: Allows unauthorized cross-origin reading of inventory balances and requisition details.
